title: Kitaev honeycomb model
intro: H = -sum K_g sigma^g sigma^g on x, y, z bonds (Pauli units unless stated).

questions.question: Which operators commute with the Kitaev Hamiltonian on every hexagon?
options: W_p = sigma^x sigma^y sigma^z sigma^x sigma^y sigma^z (outward bond labels)
questions.explanation: W_p uses on each vertex the Pauli of the bond pointing out of the hexagon; it commutes with every bond term, so the fluxes are conserved Z2 numbers.

questions.question: In Kitaev's representation sigma^a_j = i b^a_j c_j, what physical constraint must states satisfy?
options: b^x b^y b^z c = 1 on every site (D_j = 1)
questions.explanation: The Majorana space is 4-dimensional per site; D_j = 1 projects onto the 2 physical states. qslab enforces prod_j D_j = 1 exactly (Pfaffian parity).

questions.question: Lieb's theorem implies the ground state of the Kitaev model lies in which flux sector (for large clusters)?
questions.explanation: Flux-free. Tiny clusters can violate this, e.g. 2x2 where the ED ground state has W_p = -1.

questions.question: Ground-state energy per site of the isotropic Kitaev model (K = 1, Pauli units) in the thermodynamic limit?
Same model written with spin operators, H = K sum S^g S^g (|K| = 1): energy per site?
questions.explanation: S = sigma/2 so energies divide by 4: -0.7873/4 = -0.1968.

questions.question: Exact ground-state energy per site of the 18-site (3x3 cells) torus, K = 1?
questions.explanation: ED and the projected Majorana solution agree: -14.29150/18.

questions.question: Nearest-neighbour correlation <sigma^g_i sigma^g_j> on a g-bond (isotropic, TL)?
questions.explanation: Hellmann-Feynman: E/N = -(3/2) K <sigma sigma>, so <sigma sigma> = 0.7873/1.5. All further-neighbour spin correlations vanish exactly.

questions.question: Energy cost of a pair of adjacent visons (flip one u_jk), isotropic K = 1, large cluster?
questions.explanation: ~0.26 K: the flux gap is small compared with the Majorana bandwidth (6 K).

questions.question: For (Kx, Ky, Kz) = (0.2, 0.2, 1) the system is in
options: a gapped A_z phase equivalent to the toric code
questions.explanation: |Kz| > |Kx| + |Ky| violates the triangle inequality: Majoranas gap out and 4th-order perturbation theory gives the toric code.

questions.question: Adding the 3-spin term kappa (from a [111] magnetic field) to the B phase gives
options: a gapped chiral phase with Majorana Chern number +-1 (Ising anyons)
questions.explanation: kappa opens a Majorana gap Delta ~ 6 sqrt(3) kappa; Chern number +-1 means half-quantised thermal Hall kappa_xy/T = (pi/12) k_B^2/hbar.

questions.question: Entropy per site on the plateau between the two specific-heat peaks (fraction of ln 2)?
questions.explanation: Itinerant Majoranas freeze out at T_H ~ 1.5 K (Pauli units; 0.375 J in spin units with J = 4K), but the Z2 fluxes only order at T_L ~ 0.05 K (0.012 J): half of ln 2 survives in between.
